checks.actualAlgorithm: Push new items to an input stack. When the output stack is empty, transfer all input items into it; this reverses their order once.
checks.correctness: The output stack top is always the oldest remaining item. Transfer is performed only when it is empty, so newer items never pass older ones. Each item is moved at most once.
checks.workedTrace: Enqueue 4 and 9 into the incoming stack. The first Dequeue moves them to the outgoing stack and removes 4. Enqueue 2 without moving the still-pending 9. The next Dequeue removes 9; only then does transferring the incoming stack expose 2. The returned values are 4, 9 and 2 in FIFO order. JSON supplies [operationNames,argumentLists] for one fresh QueueTwoStacks. Void operations display null; Dequeue displays the returned item or {"error":"empty"}.

checks.timeDerivation: O(1) amortized per operation: each item is pushed to incoming, transferred once, then popped from outgoing. A single transfer-triggering Dequeue can cost O(q); m operations cost O(m).
checks.spaceDerivation: O(q) persistent space: each of q queued occurrences lives in exactly one of the two stacks.
